shapes.name: Google Shape;143;p3
shapes.text:
Super Micro Computer (NASDAQ: SMCI) designs, manufactures, and sells high-performance server and storage solutions for AI/ML, cloud, enterprise, and edge workloads
Founded in 1993 by Charles Liang (current CEO/Chairman) in San Jose, CA; vertically integrated with in-house motherboard design, chassis manufacturing, and system assembly
Fastest-growing server OEM globally, riding unprecedented AI infrastructure demand to $40B+ in projected FY2026 revenue
"Building Block Solutions" modular architecture enables rapid customization at scale with 6-12 week time-to-market vs. 6-12 months for Dell/HPE
Industry leader in Direct Liquid Cooling (DLC) rack-scale solutions, the fastest-growing product line as GPU power densities make air cooling inadequate

shapes.text:

shapes.text:

$13B+ Blackwell Ultra backlog provides 3+ quarters of forward revenue visibility

shapes.name: Google Shape;160;p5
shapes.text:
Global AI server TAM projected to grow from ~$125B (2024) to $400B+ (2028) at ~34% CAGR, driven by LLM training, enterprise AI deployment, and sovereign AI initiatives
Liquid cooling solutions are the fastest-growing sub-segment: ~$5B (2024) to ~$25B (2028) at ~50% CAGR as power densities exceed 100kW/rack
NVIDIA GPU roadmap (H100 to H200 to B200 to GB200 NVL72) drives sustained upgrade demand; each generation increases rack power from ~40kW to ~120kW
AI server market set to grow 55% in 2025 alone to ~$252B (Bloomberg Intelligence); hyperscaler capex budgets continuing to expand
GPT-5 class models require 10x+ the compute of GPT-4; AI inference workloads projected to exceed training by 2027

shapes.name: Text 12
shapes.text:
Speed is the core differentiator: When NVIDIA launches a new GPU, SMCI has validated designs within weeks vs. 6-12 months for Dell/HPE. In a market where every quarter of delay = lost AI training revenue, this speed premium is substantial
Dell ($104B TTM rev) has a massive enterprise sales force and full-stack solutions; HPE ($34B) has strong gov't relationships and GreenLake as-a-service. Both are investing aggressively in liquid cooling.
ODMs (Quanta, Wistron, Foxconn) build custom hyperscaler designs at 4-6% margins with no brand/IP; in-house designs (Google TPU, Amazon Trainium) are a long-term structural threat to all OEMs
SMCI holds ~25-30% share in liquid cooling specifically (market leader) but margins (6-11%) are well below Dell (20-21%) and HPE (30-32%), reflecting a volume/speed model vs. premium pricing

shapes.name: Google Shape;206;p7
shapes.text: Thesis 1: AI INFRASTRUCTURE PICK & SHOVEL PLAY

shapes.name: Google Shape;209;p7
shapes.text:
SMCI is the purest-play public equity on the AI infrastructure buildout: FY2026 revenue guided to $40B+ (from $22B in FY2025), a feat no other server OEM can match
$13B+ Blackwell Ultra backlog provides 3+ quarters of revenue visibility; GB200 NVL72 rack-scale deployments carry ~$3M+ ASPs per system
AI server TAM growing at ~34% CAGR through 2028 to $400B+; SMCI holds ~15-20% market share in GPU servers with clear leadership in liquid cooling (~25-30%)
NVIDIA partnership depth: Early access to Blackwell/GB200 platforms; first OEM to ship GB200 NVL72 rack-scale systems, demonstrating engineering trust
Catalyst: NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra production ramp in H1 CY2026 validates demand sustainability and converts backlog to recognized revenue

shapes.name: Google Shape;222;p7
shapes.text:
Direct Liquid Cooling (DLC) is transitioning from optional to mandatory as GPU power densities exceed 100kW/rack; SMCI is the acknowledged market leader with broadest product line
DLC attachment rates expected to increase from ~20% today to ~60-70% by 2028, expanding SMCI's addressable market within the broader AI server ecosystem
GB200 NVL72 requires liquid cooling by design (100% attach rate on NVIDIA's flagship platform); liquid-cooled systems create deeper switching costs (piping, manifolds, CDU infrastructure)
SMCI's DLC patents and thermal engineering expertise provide 12-18 month technology lead over Dell/HPE; rack-scale solutions carry higher ASPs than air-cooled equivalents
Risk: Dell and HPE investing heavily in DLC capabilities; technology gap could narrow within 18-24 months as competition intensifies

shapes.name: Google Shape;230;p10
shapes.text:
Margin compression driven by: (1) competitive hyperscale pricing, (2) product mix shift to lower-margin complete rack solutions, (3) component cost pass-through dynamics
Key test: Q3 FY2026 gross margin. Below 7% = margin recovery thesis weakens significantly; above 8% = bullish inflection signal
Our view: Margins likely stabilize at 8-10% over 12-18 months but will NOT return to 15-18% pre-AI era. Business model has structurally shifted toward high-volume, lower-margin.

cells: EY resigned Oct 2024; BDO appointed Nov 2024

shapes.name: Text 11
shapes.text:
The EY auditor resignation citing 'integrity' concerns is unprecedented for a company of this size; BDO's adverse opinion on internal controls as of June 30, 2024 remains the most serious qualitative risk to the investment thesis
DOJ investigation remains open with no timeline for resolution; prior 2020 SEC settlement creates pattern risk and regulators may pursue more aggressively (potential $50M-$500M penalties based on precedents)
Mitigant: Special Committee found 'no evidence of misconduct'; BDO validated financial statements with no restatements required; board reconstituted with majority independent directors
Catalyst (positive): DOJ closing investigation without charges + clean internal controls opinion from BDO = significant de-risking and potential 30%+ re-rating
Catalyst (negative): Enforcement action, executive departures, or further accounting restatements could trigger 50%+ downside as institutional holders exit positions

shapes.name: Text 12
shapes.text:
Revenue: FY2026 per mgmt guidance; FY2027-29 reflects AI capex cycle deceleration (30% to 15% to 10%) as base effect increases
Gross Margin: Troughs at ~8% in FY2026 then recovers via DLC mix shift to 40%+ of rev, pricing normalization, and next-gen product margin improvement
OpEx Leverage: R&D + SG&A decline from 3.5% to 3.2% of rev due to scale; drives operating margin from 4.5% to 7.8% over forecast period
FCF: Turns positive FY2027 as inventory normalizes from $6B+ to 40-45 days COGS; scales to ~5% FCF margin by FY2029; CapEx 1.2-1.5% of rev (Malaysia/Taiwan expansion)

shapes.name: Google Shape;279;g2b6e027a1db_6_0
shapes.text:
SMCI is arguably the most direct public equity beneficiary of AI development: every LLM trained and every inference served requires server hardware that SMCI manufactures
AI compute scaling follows a 10x+ rule per model generation (GPT-3 to GPT-4 to GPT-5); this exponential demand directly drives SMCI's $40B+ FY2026 revenue trajectory
NVIDIA's GPU roadmap (H100 → B200 → GB200 → Rubin) creates recurring upgrade cycles; each generation requires new server platforms = repeat design wins for SMCI
Liquid cooling becomes mandatory as AI model scale increases rack power from 40kW to 120kW+; SMCI's DLC leadership (25-30% share) scales directly with AI complexity
Enterprise AI adoption is in early innings: only ~5% of enterprises have deployed production AI infrastructure, implying 10-20x expansion of addressable market through 2030

shapes.name: Google Shape;281;g2b6e027a1db_6_0
shapes.text:
Custom silicon threat: Google (TPUs), Amazon (Trainium), Microsoft (Maia) designing in-house AI chips that bypass OEMs; if 30%+ of AI compute shifts to custom silicon, SMCI's TAM contracts materially
AI efficiency breakthroughs: Model distillation, mixture-of-experts, and sparse architectures could reduce compute per unit of AI capability, slowing hardware demand
Commoditization risk: Software-defined DC architectures could reduce hardware differentiation; SMCI's speed advantage may erode as workloads standardize
Geopolitical: US export controls on AI chips to China (~22% APAC rev) could intensify; sovereign AI may partially offset
